previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 15th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with only mild nausea, managed with anti-emetics. Methotrexate cleared appropriately with no renal or hepatic toxicity. An MRI showed stable lymphoma without new lesions. Her dyspnea was attributed to acute bronchitis, and she improved with a new albuterol-ipratropium inhaler. Aspirin was held during admission to enhance methotrexate excretion and was restarted at discharge. She remained stable emotionally, denying depression or suicidal ideation, and was discharged home in good condition with follow-up instructions.

# CNS lymphoma: Restaging brain MRI ___ stable.  Given cycle 
#16 high-dose MTX 8g/m2 despite lower 24hr creatinine clearance 
at 83mL/min (suspect lab error given stability of creatinine.  
Will repeat 24hr creatinine clearance with next cycle.  
Alkalinization by sodium acetate IV fluids (no IV bicarb due to 
national shortage) and PO bicarb.  Leucovorin rescue to start 
24hrs after MTX given.  Followed MTX levels daily starting 24hrs 
after MTX given.  Home when MTX <0.20.  Anti-emetics pre-meds 
and PRN.  Unclear what the cause of her pruritic episode and if 
the diphenhydramine she was given actually helped.  She has 
tolerated lorazepam numerous times over the last year.  
Reordered lorazepam PRN for nausea.  Stopped mesalamine PO so 
methotrexate excretion is not prolonged.  GI consulted and 
started mesalamine PR.  She tolerated this cycle very well with 
mild nausea.  Repeat 24hr creatinine clearance with next cycle.
